one_line: Product already in use at 0:00, a first-person bought-it line, and a named buying moment: moving up to first grade.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 wide, high angle: a woman and a boy at a marble table over an open workbook, she points, he leans in with a pencil. Voiceover (transcript): "איזה כיף זה ללמוד בצורה מקצועית". No on-screen text.
q1_hook.why: A real child working on a page is a concrete picture, and a voice starts at 0:00 (H4). But the line is a general feeling, not a problem or a result, and the product is only named at 0:08 (H1, H2). Nothing is written on screen, so a muted viewer gets no hook (H6).

beats.what: Wide static shot: mother points at pages, boy writes; voiceover praises a workbook for language and maths
beats.why: Shows real use at once, but the claim is general

beats.what: Boy cuts a paper strip with green scissors; voiceover quotes the author on the move to first grade
beats.why: Names the life moment, over a long static take

beats.what: Blurry zoom into a close-up: boy writes in boxes beside fruit pictures, mother points
beats.why: First close view of an actual exercise

beats.what: Pages of shapes and patterns; mother's hand gestures; "אני סופר ממליצה, באמת באמת" (transcript)
beats.why: Variety of exercises plus a direct recommendation

beats.what: Close-ups of the boy's head over a letters and circles page; voiceover says it is time to buy
beats.why: Spoken ask lands while a new page is shown

beats.what: Boy writes on a counting page, talks to his mother; "אתם תראו את השינוי באופן מיידי" (transcript)
beats.why: Ends on the child at work with a promise

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. The caption's "מה הכי כיף בחוברת?" is answered in the next line, so it is not a comment prompt. No save, share or tag ask.
q2_flow.why: After 0:14 the picture changes with every page, which keeps it moving (R3, E2). The first 14 s are one static take under voiceover that reads general claims, the sagging stretch (R3, R1). No reveal or reaction closes the Reel, so the ending is a pencil close-up, not a peak (R4). 44 s fits a single demo (R2).

q3_cta.what: Spoken, about 0:31 to 0:38 (transcript): "אם הילד שלכם עולה לכיתה א', זה הזמן לרכוש את החוברת". Nothing on screen. Caption end: "לפרטים נוספים ולרכישה", the author's name and a phone number.
q3_cta.why: One action, buy this workbook, said and repeated in the caption (C1). It comes after the product was shown and names who should act (C6). But it is never written on screen, and the only way to act is a phone number in the caption: friction.

q4_shown.what: A mother and her son, about 5 to 6, working through the workbook at a table: symbol tables, shape rows, a letters page, counting dots. No cover, no author name, no price. The voiceover says she bought it ("שרכשתי מדנה", transcript).
q4_shown.why: The product is handled from frame one (S1). A parent says she bought it herself, first-hand vouching (S6), though she reads the author's own words ("כמו שהיא כותבת לנו להורים", transcript). A face is not needed here (S4). The child's face is on camera but not named (S5).

q5_edit.what: 23 detected cuts in 44 s, but the first 14.5 s is one static take. Later cuts are mostly zooms and motion blur on a handheld camera (blur at 0:15 and 0:25). Voiceover runs 0:00 to 0:43 with no text. Ends on a pencil close-up.
q5_edit.why: A long static opening gives the first 3 s no cut or new picture (E1). Later zooms and blur add motion but also soften the page (E2). Voice carries everything and nothing is written, so it fails muted viewers (E4). It stops right after the last line (E8).

q6_topic.what: A mother recommends a learning workbook for children about to start first grade; serves parents worried about readiness for school.
q6_topic.why: The move from gan to first grade is a real parent concern and a buying moment, and the Reel names it (K6, K7). The claim "אתם תראו את השינוי באופן מיידי" (transcript) is strong, not modest or checkable (K4). No joy or surprise peak (K1).

q7_filmed.what: Phone on the far side of a marble table, high angle, wide at first then handheld push-ins; mother's face partly cut at the frame edge, boy leaning over the book; grey wall, even indoor light. Nobody speaks to the lens.
q7_filmed.why: A home table and phone footage look native (H8, F7). The book faces the people, so its print reads upside down to the viewer and stays small (F5, F4). The mother's face is cut by the right edge (F2). The voice is not tied to a face (F6).

q8_text.on_screen: None. No headline, no subtitles, no labels, no logo, no CTA text. The only Hebrew is the workbook's own print, upside down to the viewer and too small to read.
q8_text.caption: "חוברת מקדמת למידה לגילאי 5-6." About 50 words: a contents list (language, maths, fine motor skills), a self-answered question, a line on "הטיפ של דנה" on each page, contact line with a phone number. No hashtags, no disclosure.
q8_text.why: About 40 s of voiceover has no matching text, so a muted viewer gets nothing (T1, T3). The first caption line is a plain description with product and age, good for search, but it has no hashtags and omits first grade, the occasion the voice names (T7). No Hebrew disclosure words appear (T8).

weak_points: A read-aloud script over a long static take; book text upside down to the viewer; no cover or title shown; nothing written on screen; the only next step is a phone number in the caption.
lumebook_takeaway: Prop the phone so the open book faces the lens upright, hands turning pages, with short on-screen lines instead of a read-aloud script.
not_verified: Whether the voiceover is the mother's own voice; price; whether the mother was paid or gifted (voiceover says bought, a collab co-author is in the media data, no paid label). Corrections to coded file: cta_type is not a DM, the caption gives a phone number and no comment or DM word; shot count is 23 cuts per the index, many are zoom or blur artifacts.
